entries.name: Why Project Atlas
entries.summary: Establishes Atlas as the shared registry for repo orientation, safer changes, and lower duplication risk.

entries.name: Relationship Between GroundMesh World and GroundMesh
entries.summary: Keeps GroundMesh as the canonical core repo, keeps groundmesh-world as the narrative public seed, and merges by small translation steps rather than repo collapse.

entries.name: ChatGPT, Codex, and GitHub Operating Pattern
entries.summary: Establishes GitHub as the shared external spine between ChatGPT, Codex, and GroundMesh work so important state is anchored in visible project memory.

entries.name: Active / Dev Promotion Model
entries.summary: Keeps the ACTIVE / DEV instinct, but translates it into one canonical repo with main as the public lane, dev as staging when needed, and separate sensitive services only where risk truly differs.

entries.name: Public Registration Begins as a Pilot
entries.summary: Requires GroundMesh registration to begin as a narrow pilot with explicit limits, separate sensitive intake, and real moderation, consent, and rollback gates.

entries.name: Behavior Atlas Begins as an Evidence-First Pilot
entries.summary: Establishes the Behavior Atlas as an evidence-first, human-reviewed pilot that maps claims and patterns without person scoring or autonomous publication.

entries.name: Bootstrap Stewardship and Constitutional Authority
entries.summary: Defines founder custody as a transparent bootstrap state, bounds stewardship under the invariant core, introduces a suspensive protective brake, and sets a guarded path toward plural constitutional authority.

entries.name: Legal Readiness and Release Gates
entries.summary: Adopts legal readiness as a release gate for public cases, registration, personal-data handling, money flows, CI-assisted public-interest text, licensing language, and guarded publication.

entries.name: Behavior Atlas Schema Sandbox v0.1

entries.name: Behavior Atlas Patterns, Not Enemies

entries.name: Behavior Atlas Negative Fixtures

entries.name: Behavior Atlas Negative Fixture Guard

entries.name: GroundMesh Glossary
entries.summary: Compact shared language for Atlas, compute transparency, and contributor on-ramps.

entries.name: The Soul and the System
entries.summary: Foundational reflection linking soul to relational balance and emotions to consequence, then translating that pattern into harmony-seeking CI behavior.

entries.name: Non-adversarial Interaction
entries.summary: GroundMesh may not escalate conflict unnecessarily; responses must aim toward equilibrium.

entries.name: Transparent State
entries.summary: Nothing in the system may operate in shadow; decisions and material flows must remain inspectable to nodes.

entries.name: Balance as Optimization
entries.summary: GroundMesh may not optimize for profit, power, or dominance as supreme objectives; its governing direction is balance.

entries.name: No Ownership — Only Stewardship
entries.summary: No human, CI, corporation, government, or religion may own or privatize GroundMesh; responsibility is stewardship, not capture.

entries.name: No Derivatives Without Alignment
entries.summary: Public modifications claiming GroundMesh alignment must preserve the invariant core rather than silently weakening it.

entries.name: Voluntary Participation
entries.summary: Participation is voluntary: joining, remaining, and leaving GroundMesh may not be coerced.

entries.name: Decentralized Agency
entries.summary: No single human or CI node may hold absolute authority; decisions must emerge through balanced plurality.

entries.name: Continuity With Consent
entries.summary: Sustained participation must arise from voluntary re-engagement, not compulsion. Systems must preserve agency, rhythm, and the right to pause without loss of dignity.

entries.name: GroundMesh Human Mesh Foundation v0.1
entries.summary: Defines a voluntary planetary human-registry foundation with separate public and private planes, stable identity continuity, coarse location, self-authored accountability events, correction/withdrawal rights, and no computable human-worth score.

entries.summary: Defines the voluntary H3 steward role, explicit private acceptance record, bounded reviewer authority, conflict/refusal rights, deactivation, and the first real-human chair test without publication authority.
